findings.issue_text: Public group-members route is limited to 50 members but the members template has no pagination or load-more UI, so larger groups silently display only the first 50 members.
totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing an extra empty page when the member count is an exact multiple of the page size.
Concurrent findMembers requests can resolve out of order and overwrite offset and members, causing rapid pagination to display an older page than the selected one.

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group-members route is limited to 50 members but the members template has no pagination or load-more UI, so larger groups silently display only the first 50 members.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the public group members route (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6) calls model.findMembers() which has a default limit of 50. The template group/members.hbs iterates over 'members' but there's no pagination UI added for the public-facing group members page. The admin group page does have pagination controls (previous/next buttons with currentPage/totalPages), but the public group/members.hbs template only has a simple table with no pagination controls. This means public group member lists will only show the first 50 members with no way to see more.
